extracted.intended_audience: Python users (data scientists, educators, developers) who want to create mathematical animations with Manim
extracted.subtask_description: A hands-on tutorial for creating mathematical animations using the Manim Community Python package: installing Manim, writing Scene classes, creating Mobjects, applying animations, camera control, graphs, grouping, and tracing paths. Focuses on practical examples and command-line rendering flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Manim Community version
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the Manim Community version is updated more frequently and better tested, use it for the tutorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the Documentation for dependencies and install with: pip install manim. The page explicitly contrasts the original Grant Sanderson version vs the community-maintained version and recommends the latter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene: use construct() and play()
rubrics_metrics.description: Scene is the base class providing animation infrastructure via construct() and play() methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a class inheriting from Scene and implement construct() to create and animate Mobjects using self.play(...). Use self.wait() for timed pauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and configure Mobjects (Square, Circle, Dot, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobjects are objects that can be displayed on the screen, such as Circle, Square, Matrix, Angle, Dot, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instantiate shapes (e.g., Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)). Use methods like set_fill(color, opacity) and rotate(angle) to style and orient Mobjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animations: use Create, Transform, GrowFromCenter, FadeOut, Write, MoveAlongPath, ReplacementTransform, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Animations are operations applied to Mobjects such as Write, Create, GrowFromCenter, Transform, FadeOut that control how objects appear, morph, or disappear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Create to draw shapes, GrowFromCenter to animate growth from center, Transform to morph one object into another, Write to animate text as handwriting, and FadeOut to remove objects smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render command-line flags and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Use manim command flags to control rendering behavior and output format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: manim -p -ql start.py GrowingSquare ( -p = play after rendering, -ql = low quality ). For high quality use -qh. To create a GIF add --format=gif. To get an image of the last frame add -s (manim -p -qh -s more.py Graph).

rubrics_metrics.name: MathTex for LaTeX equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MathTex to create mathematical equations using LaTeX notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a raw string (r"...") for LaTeX commands. Example: equation = MathTex(r"e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0"); animate with self.play(Write(equation)). Break multi-part equations into separate MathTex arguments to access parts individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight parts with SurroundingRectangle and ReplacementTransform
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SurroundingRectangle to add a moving frame/highlight around parts of an equation and ReplacementTransform to switch highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create framebox = SurroundingRectangle(equation[index], buff=.1). Use ReplacementTransform(framebox1, framebox2) to animate the frame moving from one part to another. buff controls spacing between box and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: MovingCameraScene and camera.frame.animate for zooming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MovingCameraScene to allow camera movement and self.camera.frame to control zoom and centering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(equation[0])) to zoom in (scale <1) and center on a specific submobject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axes and plotting graphs with labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Axes to create coordinate grids and axes.plot to draw functions, plus labeling helpers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instantiate axes with x_range, y_range, x_length, y_length. Add axis labels via axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)"). Plot functions with axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=BLUE) and label graphs with axes.get_graph_label(graph, label="x^2").

rubrics_metrics.name: Use self.add vs self.play appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: self.add instantly displays objects on screen without animating them; self.play performs animated transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self.add for immediate placement (e.g., adding axes before animating a graph), and self.play to animate creation or transformations so viewers see the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group objects with VGroup and manipulate together
rubrics_metrics.description: Group multiple Mobjects using VGroup so they behave as a single unit for arrangement and movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create group = VGroup(obj1, obj2); use group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=1) to layout, and group.animate.shift(UP*2) to move the entire group. You can combine groups and animate subsets independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use arrange, shift and basic transforms for layout and movement
rubrics_metrics.description: arrange(direction, buff) lines up objects; shift(vector) moves objects by vector multiples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=1) arranges horizontally with 1 unit spacing; shift(UP*2) moves object two units up.

rubrics_metrics.name: TracedPath for drawing trails of moving objects
rubrics_metrics.description: TracedPath creates a path that follows a moving object's position, producing a trail/pen effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=BLUE, stroke_width=4) and add it with the moving dot; use MoveAlongPath to animate the dot and rate_func/run_time to control motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: MoveAlongPath and rate_func/run_time control motion timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MoveAlongPath to animate movement along a path and rate_func/run_time to change speed/profile and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, Circle(radius=2)), rate_func=linear, run_time=4) moves at constant speed for 4 seconds. rate_func controls easing.

rubrics_metrics.name: add_updater for continuous per-frame updates
rubrics_metrics.description: add_updater attaches a function to an object so it updates every frame (useful for rotation or dynamic behaviors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rolling_circle.add_updater(lambda m: m.rotate(-0.3)) makes the circle rotate automatically each frame while it moves, enabling rolling effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fill and stroke properties (set_fill, color, fill_opacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Style shapes by setting fill color and opacity and by specifying stroke color via constructor or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., circle.set_fill(PINK, opacity=0.5) for 50% transparent fill. Pass color=BLUE to constructors for stroke color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rotate(angle) to orient Mobjects
rubrics_metrics.description: rotate(angle) rotates an object by the given angle (radians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: square.rotate(PI/4) to rotate a square by 45 degrees before animating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive transformations for step-by-step solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Show multi-step equation transformations by writing the first equation and then Transform-ing it through intermediate steps to the final result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example workflow: self.play(Write(step1)); self.play(Transform(step1, step2)); self.play(Transform(step1, step3)) with waits between to pace teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame extraction: use -s to save last frame image
rubrics_metrics.description: Add -s to the manim command to produce an image of the scene's final frame instead of a video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: manim -p -qh -s more.py Graph. Useful for static illustrations or thumbnails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples + GitHub/Jupyter for reproducible learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full source code and Jupyter notebooks so readers can clone and follow along.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial supplies a GitHub repo and Jupyter notebook; cloning and running examples accelerates learning and experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera background customization via self.camera.background_color
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the scene background color using self.camera.background_color (e.g., WHITE instead of default black).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set background at start of construct() to affect entire scene: self.camera.background_color = WHITE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use get_axis_labels and get_graph_label for clear annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Add axis and graph labels programmatically to make plots self-explanatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)") and axes.get_graph_label(graph, label="x^2") to attach readable labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Scene types (Scene vs MovingCameraScene)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose Scene subclass based on needed capabilities: general Scene for static camera, MovingCameraScene when camera movement/zoom required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MovingCameraScene when you need self.camera.frame.animate.scale(...) or other camera animations; otherwise Scene suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recap classification: three core Manim concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim programming revolves around three kinds of objects: Mobjects, Scenes, and Animations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design animations by creating Mobjects, placing them on Scenes, and applying Animations. Understanding this separation helps structure code and debugging.
